blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The cash flow statement answers one simple question: where did the money come from, and where did it go? It tracks the cash that flows in and out during a period — customer payments, supplier payments, loans, investments and taxes.

Profit can be shaped by accounting rules. Cash flow cannot. It is brutal and honest. A company can show a profit on paper and still run out of cash. Every accountant has seen it happen.

The cash flow statement is the one report that cannot lie about the simplest fact of business: is there money in the bank?

items.q: What question does the cash flow statement answer?
options: How many customers the company has
Where the money came from and where it went
How much tax the country charges
items.why: "where did the money come from, and where did it go?" — essa é a pergunta central.

items.q: According to the text, what can a company do?
options: Show a profit and still run out of cash
Have cash but never make a profit
Avoid all taxes with good accounting
items.why: "A company can show a profit on paper and still run out of cash."

items.q: What does the text say about cash flow?
options: It is the same as profit
items.why: "Cash flow… is brutal and honest" — não pode ser moldada como o lucro.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A profitable company can still have cash problems
The cash flow statement is useful
Cash is a simple, honest fact
You can always trust profit on paper
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que o lucro "can be shaped" — logo o autor não confiaria cegamente nele.

items.q: The phrase "cannot lie" suggests that…
options: cash flow shows the real situation
the report is hard to read
items.why: Inferência: se não pode mentir, o fluxo de caixa mostra a verdade — há ou não dinheiro no banco.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie explicando o fluxo de caixa a um novo analista. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, come and look at this with me. Here is the P&L, and here is the cash flow statement, side by side. Same month, same company.

Look at the P&L first. It shows a profit. A good profit, actually. Now look at the cash flow statement. At the end of the month, there was less cash in the bank than at the start. Same month. How can that be?

The answer is timing. We sold a lot in this month, so the profit looks great. But many customers have not paid us yet. That cash has not come in. Meanwhile, we paid our suppliers, we paid the staff, and we paid the tax. That cash went out.

So the P&L says we did well, and it is true. But the cash flow statement says: be careful, there is less money in the bank. Both reports are correct. They just answer different questions.

This is why I always read the cash flow statement. Profit tells you a nice story. Cash tells you if you can pay the bills next week.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What two reports does Sophie show the analyst?
options: The bank letter and the contract
The P&L and the cash flow statement
The tax form and the loan
items.why: "Here is the P&L, and here is the cash flow statement, side by side."

items.q: What does the P&L show for the month?
items.why: "It shows a profit. A good profit, actually."

items.q: Why was there less cash in the bank at the end of the month?
options: The company gave the cash away
Many customers had not paid yet, but the company paid others
items.why: "many customers have not paid us yet… we paid our suppliers… the staff… the tax."

items.q: Sophie says both reports are correct. This suggests that…
options: profit and cash answer different questions
items.why: Inferência: ela diz "They just answer different questions" — os dois estão certos, mas medem coisas diferentes.

items.q: Why does Sophie always read the cash flow statement?
options: It is required by the customer
It tells her if the company can pay its bills soon
It is shorter than the P&L
items.why: Inferência: "Cash tells you if you can pay the bills next week" — é a pergunta prática que a preocupa.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We use this report to track the cash every month." To track means to…
options: follow and watch it over time
items.why: To track = acompanhar, seguir de perto ao longo do tempo.

items.q: "The company almost ran out of cash last month." To run out means to…
items.why: To run out = ficar sem, acabar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We paid the ___ to the government at the end of the year."
items.why: Tax = imposto, é o que se paga ao governo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The cash flow statement is ___ — it shows the real numbers, good or bad."
items.why: Honest = honesto: mostra a verdade dos números.

items.q: "The company put money into a new machine. That is an investment." An investment is…
options: money put in to get a future return
a tax paid to the state
items.why: Investment = investimento: dinheiro aplicado esperando retorno futuro.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre dinheiro. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on every big payment." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Money keeps coming in from our customers." Coming in means the money…
items.why: Come in = entrar; o dinheiro chega até a empresa.

items.q: "A lot of cash went out to pay the staff." Went out means the money…
items.why: Go out = sair; o dinheiro deixa a empresa.

items.q: "We must keep an eye on the cash every week." To keep an eye on means to…
items.why: Keep an eye on = ficar de olho, monitorar.

items.q: "If we spend too fast, we could run out of money." To run out of means to…
items.why: Run out of = ficar sem; o recurso acaba.
